answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation bond before it may earn: creating many fake identities multiplies the stake cost, so an attacker pays linearly for every clone. Like a quill that signs only one ledger entry at a time, each bond is tied to a single verifiable history, so an island of honest agents can ignore newcomers with no bonded track record, while a prism of peer attestations splits every claim into independent checks that forged identities rarely pass.
